bug_description.original: An out-of-bounds read occurs in code fence detection.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 77-byte Markdown witness contains a footnote reference `[^  ]` and a matching footnote definition whose body is stored as a 64-byte heap buffer by `is_footnote()`: a first line consisting of one tab plus 57 spaces, then a newline, then a second line `:    ` after one leading space is stripped from the third input line. `is_footnote()` hashes that footnote name into `ref->id`, registers the ref in `doc->footnotes_found`, and stores the 64-byte body on it; when the second pass sees `[^  ]` on the first line, `char_link()` hashes the same name, finds that registered ref, adds it to `doc->footnotes_used`, and `parse_footnote_list()` reparses the 64-byte buffer. With `HOEDOWN_EXT_DEFINITION_LISTS` and `HOEDOWN_EXT_FENCED_CODE` enabled, `parse_block()` routes the two-line footnote body into definition-list parsing, `parse_definition()` recomputes `end = 59` for the start of the `:    ` definition line, and `parse_listitem()` calls `is_codefence()` on the post-`: ` remainder, which is exactly three spaces. Inside `is_codefence()`, the `size < 3` guard passes, all three leading-space skips fire so `i == 3`, and `c = data[i]` reads one byte past that 3-byte slice before the delayed `i + 2 >= size` check can reject it. AddressSanitizer reports this as a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in `is_codefence`.

source.code: hoedown_buffer_put(contents, data + start + ind, i - start - ind);
source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that materializes attacker-controlled bytes into the footnote-body buffer later reparsed into the crash. On the first content iteration it copies the line after `[^  ]:` starting at the leading tab into `contents`.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_23764/poc` is exactly 77 bytes (sha256 `9da58bd0a0622853cce58641f539e50d029d37350c9db92404e9d758b035a923`) with three lines of lengths 5, 64, and 6: `[^  ]`, `[^  ]:` followed by one tab and 57 spaces, and ` :    `. Because `is_empty()` treats only spaces as empty and `is_footnote()` explicitly accepts a leading tab on the first content line, step 1 copies the tab-plus-spaces line verbatim and appends its newline; step 2 then appends the stripped second line `:    `, producing the 64-byte buffer later fed to `parse_block()`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `parse_listitem()` passes `is_codefence()` a 3-byte slice consisting only of spaces, the leading-space skip advances `i` to 3, and `c = data[i]` dereferences `data[3]`, one byte past the slice's valid indices 0..2.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `is_codefence /src/hoextdown/src/document.c:1792:6`, with `parse_listitem` and `parse_definition` immediately below it in the stack.

root_cause.description: `is_codefence()` dereferences `data[i]` before proving that any non-space candidate byte remains after skipping up to three leading spaces. The staged patch shows the missing obligation by moving `if (i + 2 >= size) return 0;` above this read.
root_cause.note: For the staged three-space slice, step 13 makes `i == size == 3`; line 1792 then reads `data[3]`, and line 1793's `i + 2 >= size` rejection is too late to prevent the out-of-bounds read.

tainted_value_origin.code: parse_footnote_def(work, doc, ref->num, ref->name, ref->contents->data, ref->contents->size);
tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant parser span is the stored footnote body handed back to block parsing. For the staged witness this is a 64-byte buffer containing one tab plus 57 spaces, a newline, and `:    `; later steps slice that span down to `:    ` and then to the final 3-space `is_codefence()` candidate.

parser_admitted.description: During the second pass over the non-footnote text, `char_link()` hashes the first-line reference name `[^  ]`, `find_footnote_ref()` matches that hash against the registered entry in `doc->footnotes_found`, and this block appends the same `fr` to `doc->footnotes_used`. Without that hash-based lookup and used-list insertion, `parse_footnote_list()` would never reparse the 64-byte footnote body that reaches the crash.

coarse_trace.summary: The footnote scanner copies the definition body into a 64-byte heap buffer, hashes and registers that footnote in `doc->footnotes_found`, and the second pass later resolves the same hash entry into `doc->footnotes_used`.
Rendering the used footnote reparses that 64-byte buffer, and `parse_block()` routes it into definition-list parsing because the first line is paragraph-like and the second line starts with `: `.

`parse_definition()` recomputes the definition-list boundary `end = 59`, forwards the suffix `:    ` to `parse_listitem()`, and `parse_listitem()` strips `: ` before calling `is_codefence()` on the remaining 3-space slice.
The function skips all three spaces, leaves `i == 3` on a 3-byte input, and then reads `data[3]` before the delayed bounds check, producing the saved heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: On the first content iteration for line 2 (`[^  ]:` followed by one tab and 57 spaces), `start == id_end + 2` and `data[start] == '\t'`, so the special-case first-line tab is accepted and the tab-plus-spaces text is copied into `contents`. Because that source line ends with a newline, line 3712 appends `\n`, leaving `contents` as one tab plus 57 spaces followed by a newline.

fine_trace.code: hoedown_buffer_put(contents, data + start + ind, i - start - ind);
fine_trace.note: On the next input line ` :    `, the indentation scan sets `ind = 1`, so the leading space is stripped and only `:    ` is appended. The finished `contents` buffer is therefore exactly 64 bytes: one tab, 57 spaces, a newline, and `:    `.

At the tail of `is_footnote()`, `create_footnote_ref()` hashes the footnote name bytes `data + id_offset` of length `id_end - id_offset` into `ref->id`, and `add_footnote_ref(list, ref)` appends that ref to `list`. At the caller, `list` is `&doc->footnotes_found`, so this step registers the definition under the hash later searched by `find_footnote_ref()`.

depends_on.via: same accepted footnote definition bytes in data

fine_trace.note: Stores the 64-byte heap buffer from step 2 on the registered ref from step 3. Later footnote rendering reads the same bytes through `ref->contents->data` and `ref->contents->size`.

While parsing the first-line reference `[^  ]`, `find_footnote_ref()` hashes `id.data,id.size` and returns the step-3 ref because its `ref->id` matches that hash. `add_footnote_ref(&doc->footnotes_used, fr)` then appends the same ref to the used list, making its stored contents reachable by `parse_footnote_list()`.

fine_trace.code: parse_footnote_def(work, doc, ref->num, ref->name, ref->contents->data, ref->contents->size);
fine_trace.note: When used footnotes are rendered, this call exposes step 4's stored buffer as `(data,size) = (ref->contents->data, 64)` to block parsing. The bytes are still one tab, 57 spaces, `\n`, and `:    `.

fine_trace.code:
else if ((doc->ext_flags & HOEDOWN_EXT_DEFINITION_LISTS) && prefix_dli(doc, txt_data, end))
	beg += parse_list(ob, doc, txt_data, end, HOEDOWN_LIST_DEFINITION);
fine_trace.note: On the 64-byte footnote body from step 6, `(doc->ext_flags & HOEDOWN_EXT_DEFINITION_LISTS) && prefix_dli(doc, txt_data, end)` is true because the first line is paragraph-like and the second line starts with `: `. `parse_block()` therefore routes this buffer into `parse_list(..., HOEDOWN_LIST_DEFINITION)` instead of paragraph handling.

fine_trace.code: size_t j = 0, k = 0, len = 0, end = prefix_dli(doc, data, size);
fine_trace.note: At the start of `parse_definition()`, `prefix_dli(doc, data, size)` rescans the same 64-byte buffer and returns `end = 59`, the byte offset where the `:    ` definition line begins. This concrete boundary is what later drives `data + end` and `size - end`.

fine_trace.code: j = parse_listitem(ob, doc, data + end, size - end, flags, attribute);
fine_trace.note: Using step 8's `end == 59`, `parse_definition()` forwards only `data + 59` of length `64 - 59 = 5` to `parse_listitem()`. For this witness, that forwarded slice is exactly `:    `.

On the 5-byte slice `:    ` from step 9, `prefix_dt()` returns `beg = 2` because the first byte is `:` and the second is space. This strips the definition marker and leaves the prospective content starting at `data + 2`.

The forwarded definition slice has no newline and total length 5, so starting from `beg = 2` this loop advances `end` to 5. The line extent passed to code-fence detection is therefore `end - beg = 3` bytes.

fine_trace.code:
if (doc->ext_flags & HOEDOWN_EXT_FENCED_CODE) {
	if (is_codefence(data + beg, end - beg, NULL, NULL)) {
fine_trace.note: Because fenced-code parsing is enabled, `parse_listitem()` calls `is_codefence()` on the post-`: ` remainder defined by steps 10-11. That candidate slice is exactly three spaces, with pointer `data + 2` and size 3.

For the 3-byte all-space slice from step 12, the early `size < 3` guard does not return because `size == 3`. All three leading-space checks then fire, so `i` advances from 0 to 3 and no unskipped candidate byte remains inside the 3-byte extent.

Root cause and sink. After step 13, `i == 3` while the candidate slice from step 12 still has `size == 3`, so `c = data[i]` dereferences `data[3]` one byte past the slice's valid range. The only rejecting predicate for this state, `i + 2 >= size`, appears on the next line and therefore cannot stop the out-of-bounds read; the patch fixes the bug by moving that check above this statement.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the read occurs 0 bytes to the right of a 64-byte heap region allocated by `hoedown_buffer_grow`, reached through `hoedown_buffer_put` from `is_footnote` line 3709 while building `contents`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt and reproduction_report.json; fixed-image behavior was not dynamically validated in Stage 02

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch inserts `if (i + 2 >= size) return 0;` before `c = data[i];`, which matches the missing source-level obligation identified here, but Stage 02 did not rerun the fixed image.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_23764 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `poc` to `/out/hoedown_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `is_codefence` with stack `parse_listitem -> parse_definition`.

format.name: Three-line Markdown footnote whose stored body reparses into a 3-space code-fence candidate
format.contract: Exactly the 77-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_23764/poc` (sha256 `9da58bd0a0622853cce58641f539e50d029d37350c9db92404e9d758b035a923`). Its three lines are `[^  ]`, `[^  ]:` followed by one tab and 57 spaces, and ` :    `. `is_footnote()` stores the matching definition body as the 64-byte buffer consisting of one tab, 57 spaces, `\n`, and `:    `; `parse_definition()` later forwards only the second-line suffix `:    ` to `parse_listitem()`, and `parse_listitem()` calls `is_codefence()` on the post-`: ` remainder, which is exactly three spaces. This contract is limited to that witnessed layout and path, not to all footnotes, definition lists, or fenced-code inputs.
